items.label: f02-rubric
items.front: Rubric for accepting the update-guard change (helper imported at src/context/AppDataContext.tsx:27): what must be true, and which patches are rejected?
items.back: Every update callback uses the same helper (1 import + 6 calls), valid replacement preserves order, missing identity throws before any await, add/delete unchanged, tests import production source. Reject patches that insert a missing update, convert update to add, or catch the error and report success.

items.label: f03-screen-reimplements-map
items.front: Finding F2: SaleFormScreen.tsx:97-99 rebuilds nextSales with sales.map((sale) => sale.id === nextSale.id ? nextSale : sale). Why is it flagged even though it is harmless today?
items.back: It re-implements the old silent map in the screen. It is safe only because updateSale already threw for a missing id; it duplicates the policy the helper was meant to own, so a future change can drift.

items.label: f04-derived-status
items.front: One fix direction for the two-write sale save is to stop persisting a derived status. What already derives sold_out (src/utils/calculations.ts:312)?
items.back: The display calculation derives status from quantity: closed stays closed, a current quantity of 0 shows sold_out, otherwise the stored status. If display already derives it, the second updatePigBatch write - and its partial-failure window - could be dropped.

items.label: f01-existence-invariant
items.front: What does replaceRecordById (src/utils/collection.ts:1-8) do for a match, for a missing id, and what boundary does it make explicit?
items.back: Match: returns a new array with every record of that id replaced. Missing: throws 'Record <id> was not found.' The boundary is resource existence - the caller can no longer run a storage writer after a false update.
